title: Choosing, sharpening and cleaning pruning tools for a bush rose

common.applies_to: Established Hybrid Tea, Floribunda or Grandiflora bush rose (a rose that has passed PKR-SGT-000003); dormant pruning
common.preserved_uncertainty: The thickness at which hand pruners give way to loppers differs between sources: three-quarters of an inch in two rose sources, half an inch in a general woody-plant text (C8). Sources name bypass pruners without giving a reason, and one recommends anvil pruners for dead wood (C9). Sources differ on what to disinfect with and how often, and none cites evidence of effectiveness (C10). No source compares sharp and blunt tools directly; the advice rests on practitioner agreement (AF-27).

items.text: Match the tool to the stem: bypass hand pruners for thin canes, loppers for thicker ones, and a pruning saw for the thickest or oldest canes.
Use bypass (scissor-action) pruners. Anvil pruners (which crush the stem against a flat edge) are fine for clearing dead wood only.
Keep your tools sharp and clean, so each cut is clean and doesn't crush the cane.
Clean your blades between plants, and after cutting out diseased wood, so you don't spread disease from one plant to another.
